newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent weaker as buyers opt for other grades.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent weaker as buyers opt for other grades.

text.p: Dated Brent weakened on Wednesday as refiners opted for other North Sea grades despite sharply higher premiums for specific grades, traders said.
The cash market was quite with no outright paper traded. The Oct/Nov spread was also weaker as the number of unsold October Brent cargoes held by a major weighed on the near-month spread.
CFDs for next week's dates also softened 2-3 cents and talked around Nov +8/+10 cents in the late afternoon after an earlier deal at Nov +10 cents.
A Brent cargo loading Oct 1-3 was sold at November +6 cents, down from the last deal at Nov +9 cents on Tuesday.
"Brent is still quite cheap but first decade demand is not sufficient, so logic says it is not too good," a wet trader said.
The major believed holding six Brent cargoes kept the one Brent date which turned wet on Wednesday.
The trader said that unless the arb to the U.S. opened or Brent moved out of the region, physical Brent was likely to remain weak.
Even at these levels, Brent was not tempting NWE refiners, who are mopping up other North Sea grades after a huge buying spree on Tuesday saw more than 10 million barrels traded.
There were some signs that North Sea differentials were easing from Tuesday's levels with the exception of Forties.

A Forties cargo loading October 20 traded at Dated Brent +26 cents, up six cents from Tuesday. Statfjord (Oct 15-17) came off to trade at Dated Brent +25 cents after a Tuesday deal at Dated +30 cents for an earlier cargo.
In the Med, scarce Urals traded at higher differentials. An Italian refiner picked up an Oct 1-3 cargo at Dated Brent -70 cents on Tuesday, up five cents from last week.
"There is not much sour around and nobody knows what will be the October programme," a Med trader said.
